items.body: Review by UMUR — "For the Love of Art and the Making" is the third full-length studio album by Danish power/progressive metal act Beyond Twilight (if you discount the two Twilight albums as the works ofanother band). The album was released through Massacre Records in April 2006. It�s the successor to"Section X" from March 2005. There has been one lineup change since "Section X" as lead vocalistKelly Sundown Carpenter has been replaced by Swedish singer Bj�rn Jansson."For the Love of Art and the Making" is quite an interesting release as it�s basically one, 37:49minutes long composition broken down into 43 sub tracks. Stylistically it�s a continuation of thepower/progressive metal style of the preceding releases and as Jansson is a suitable and not toodifferent sounding replacement for Carpenter, the change on the lead vocalist spot doesn�t changemuch in terms of consistency of the band�s sound. The many short sub tracks makes "For the Love ofArt and the Making" a very different listening experience though as the tracks form only short partsof a longer track, they don�t have much time to evolve.It�s not that this is simple or one-dimensional music, because the tracks often shift in dynamicsbetween a heavy power/progressive metal oriented approach and more subtle and mellow parts. A normalverse/chorus structured composition wouldn�t work that way because it�s longer and you have time todevelop ideas over the course of a longer playing time. Here the short track lengths mean that ideasare executed fast and they flow by even faster. I�m not sure I think it always work that well,because sometimes I feel Beyond Twilight could have done a lot more with some of the parts, but atthat point they have usually already moved on to the next section. So, although "For the Love of Art and the Making" is a both well produced and well performedrelease, the songwriting approach will probably divide the waters. There�s arguably a lot of qualityhere but as an album I�m not sure I think "For the Love of Art and the Making" works that well. Tomy ears it�s more a study in interesting ideas and high level musicianship. Thinking of "For theLove of Art and the Making" as a single coherent composition doesn�t cross my mind while listeningto the album. The song is constantly disrupted and changes gears and dynamics and it�s actually abit stressful to listen to. When that is said "For the Love of Art and the Making" is still a highquality release, but I�m pretty sure it�s an acquired taste, so enter at your own risk. A 3.5 star(70%) rating is deserved.(Originally posted on Metal Music Archives).
items._genre: progressive metal / power metal / experimental structure
items._cn_summary: 这张丹麦乐队作品将一首37分49秒的长篇曲目拆解为43个短小段落，在力量金属与前卫金属的基底上不断切换力度与情绪，段落之间频繁变速与转向，打破常规主歌副歌结构。评论指出制作精良、演奏水准高超，动态对比丰富，但碎片化的写作方式使得许多想法来不及展开便被下一段落取代，整体更像是一系列高水准音乐构思的集合，而非真正连贯的单一长篇。乐评对这种结构的艺术性予以肯定，但认为其作为专辑的完整性有所欠缺，聆听体验偏紧张且小众，属于需要特定偏好的听众才能接受的作品。

items.body: Virgin Birth, an industrial punk trio from Louisville, Kentucky, will release the six-song EP The Dead End on 16 October 2026 via Never Nervous Records. The band recorded the EP at The Slaughtered Lamb Studio in Louisville. The title track became available on streaming platforms on 2 October 2026, ahead of the full release. Virgin Birth is Phillip Olympia (vocals, synthesizers), Jake Miller (guitar) and Matt Haas (bass). Never Nervous Records described “The Dead End” as continuing the band’s “fascination with the darker corners of electronic music, punk, and the increasingly stupid world we all find ourselves living in.” The label said the band’s earlier releases “looked outward at collapse on a larger scale,” while the new songs are “more immediate, claustrophobic, and personal.” A music video for the title track is set to follow within the week, according to Never Nervous Records. “The Dead End” arrives digitally across major streaming platforms. More live dates and physical releases are planned through Never Nervous Records. About Virgin Birth Virgin Birth formed in Louisville as an industrial synth punk project led by Phillip Olympia and Jake Miller. The duo released its debut EP, “The Forest,” on 26 May 2023 through Never Nervous Records. The nine-track EP included backing vocals from Mandy Keathley and cover art by Albie Mason, and was mixed and mastered by Jake Miller at The Slaughtered Lamb Studio. Virgin Birth followed with the three-song EP “From Behind” on 14 April 2024, also recorded at The Slaughtered Lamb Studio. The band released “I Can’t Read” as a single in March 2025 ahead of its debut full-length album, “Total Annihilation,” issued 2 May 2025 via Never Nervous Records on digital formats and cassette. The ten-track album was again mixed and mastered by Jake Miller at The Slaughtered Lamb Studio, with Olympia handling vocals, synthesizers, drum machines and guitars, and Miller on guitars and synthesizers. Virgin Birth released the remix single “Don’t Tell Me [neu flesh remix]” in August 2025, followed the next month by “SPLIT,” a split release with Scary Black. Matt Haas joined the band on bass by June 2026, when Virgin Birth released a cover of Nirvana’s “Floyd the Barber” as a trio for the first time. “The Dead End” is Virgin Birth’s first EP since “From Behind” in 2024.
items._genre: industrial / punk / synth-punk / dark electronic
items._cn_summary: Virgin Birth 是来自美国肯塔基州路易斯维尔的三人工业朋克组合，将于2026年10月通过 Never Nervous Records 发行六首曲目的EP《The Dead End》。乐队由主唱兼合成器手 Phillip Olympia、吉他手 Jake Miller 和贝斯手 Matt Haas 组成，录音工作于路易斯维尔的 The Slaughtered Lamb Studio 完成。厂牌描述这张EP延续了乐队对电子音乐朋克阴暗角落的迷恋，主题从以往对宏观崩溃的审视转向更为即时、封闭、私密的表达。乐队此前发行过EP《From Behind》、全长专辑《Total Annihilation》，并与 Scary Black 合作发行过Split作品，还曾翻唱Nirvana的《Floyd the Barber》。本文为新闻发布性质的信息，内容以发行公告和乐队履历为主，缺乏对音乐本身的深度评析。

items.body: Review by kenethlevine — A crisp, violin and guitar led prog act can't help but invoke a certain era of a certain UK prog monarch led by ROBERT FRIPP, and this instrumental album isn't unworthy of such a parallel, but this is mostly in the distorted icy leads and the jazz inflections. With no vocals and a tendency to prefer structured jamming over improv, not to mention a folk orientation that Crimson increasingly set aside after 1972, it would be as unfair to SCARLET THREAD as it is to an obvious mentor to stretch this analogy any further. A better comparison might be Montreal's TALISMA or, originating in the HACKETT school, MR GIL/BELIEVE or HARNAKIS. Among fellow Finns, perhaps AQUAPLAN but without vocals, at least for now.As I said, this is jamming but in a disciplined and repetitive way that generally works well enough and is nothing if not appealing to prog ears, though everything seems a bit interchangeable - throw in a guitar motif, enhance with violin, maybe add flute, then move on to another violin theme, and enhance with guitar, maybe add flute, and so on. Luckily these are all well orchestrated. The opener and closer seem to hit highest on the sustainability index, along with "Siipirikon Lento" (flight of the bird with the injured wing). More would emerge in the subsequent decade, with a few dramatic changes, so this is not one of those debuts that unwittingly doubled as a swan song. Mildly recommended, but more enthusiastically for certain listener profiles.

items._cn_summary: 这张芬兰乐队的器乐专辑以小提琴和吉他为主导，呈现出结构化的即兴风格，融合了民谣导向与爵士元素。整体编曲以重复的乐器主题交替展开：小提琴与吉他动机轮番出现，辅以长笛点缀，各乐器间编排有序。虽然评论指出各曲之间存在一定程度的互换感，但首尾曲及《Siipirikon Lento》在持续性上表现最佳。专辑在演奏上保持纪律性与克制感，避免了过度即兴的松散，同时带有King Crimson式的失真吉他音色和冰冽质感。作为乐队的早期作品，它为后续十年的更具戏剧性的发展奠定了基础，呈现了一种有节制的渐进风格探索。

items.body: Karine Polwart has proved herself to be an exceptional talent as a singer and songwriter for many years, all the way back to her time with Malinky (the song �Thaney� was a revelation). As a solo artist she�s grown and continually expanded her horizons, coming now to Windblown , a project that began life seven years ago, when Polwart, along with sound designer and composer Pippa Murphy, was artist in residence at Royal Botanic Garden Edinburgh. The album, with its stage show and book, tells the story of the garden�s oldest specimen, a Sabal palm tree ( Sabal bermudana ), which was gently felled in 2021, and contained a surprise nobody had expected. The tree is the starting point. From there, imagination runs free. Windblown by Karine Polwart & Pippa Murphy featuring Dave Milligan It�s an album of voice and piano (the outstanding, sympathetic Dave Milligan), and, for all its global outlook on connections, one that�s very rooted in Scotland. You can hear it on the opening track, �Hear The Rigging/Last In Line,� where the melody becomes a slow, aching lament that would sound completely natural on the pipes. The stripped-down sound gives the songs both crafted stateliness and real intimacy. Each one is an exhalation, a memory, a celebration and exploration, with recurring phrases in the words and music acting as touchstones � or even hooks; they certainly stick in the mind. Windblown by Karine Polwart & Pippa Murphy featuring Dave Milligan In many ways, this is a modest album, with piano, voice and light, judicious soundscaping. It won�t overpower with noise. Yet at the same time, it�s epic, a look at history, at the flow and grandeur of nature, and the things we all carry within us. The music, and especially Polwart�s warm, compassionate voice, envelop the listener, and makes them a participant, not an observer, but a part of the journey and the history. Windblown by Karine Polwart & Pippa Murphy featuring Dave Milligan The irony arrives at the end, when the venerable old tree is down, and seeds are examined. What people for two hundred years had believed to be a Sabal bermudana turns out to be something different, a Sabal mexicana � and one of the small plants fill grow where it�s forerunner once stood. Windblown by Karine Polwart & Pippa Murphy featuring Dave Milligan Like music, plants keep to a different time � and this album/book/show give the tree the requiem it deserves, as well as hope for the future. items.body:
According to its founder, Eugene Rodriguez, who also sings and plays on the record, Los Cenzontles is a �musical group and non-profit organization, which I founded over thirty years ago.�  As he continues in the album�s liner notes, the group �has a long history of producing projects exploring Mexico�s deep roots and our connections with various traditions that, so far, have included Irish, Louisiana Creole, Cuban, American cowboy, classical, pop, rock, and blues�, the latest of which is
Adios Ke Aloha: Waves of the Same Sea
. Los Cenzontles translates to the mockingbird, or, from its Aztec root word, the bird of four hundred voices. This is a fitting name for the range of musical diversity represented here.
With songs sung in Spanish, Hawaiian, and English, the concept traces back to the legacy of Mexican cowboys who travelled from California to the Hawaiian Islands to wrangle the long-horned cattle introduced there in the nineteenth century. They also brought the guitar. The 16 tracks feature old Hawaiian songs with new Spanish lyrics, old Mexican songs with new Hawaiian lyrics, new compositions, and traditional Americana. Yet it is an entirely cohesive musical package held together by dense arrangements of ukuleles, guitars, Mexican harp, and accordion.
Sonny Lim & David Hidalgo
Besides their distinctive voices, the headline artists Taj Mahal and David Hidalgo provide the gravitas and musicianship that their long and distinguished careers have earned. According to the liner notes, they were the catalysts behind the project and facilitated the choice of songs, arrangements, and played a range of instruments. On vocals they are joined by Hawaiian natives Gary Haleamau, Sheldeen Haleamau, Sonny Lim, and long-time Cenzontles member Fabiola Trujillo.
Deportee
To give a taste of the sessions, included before the traditional �Fishin� Blues� is Taj Mahal teaching the musicians how to play it. Sung by David Hildalgo,  the lovely �A Matter of Time� comes from the 1984 album
Will the Wolf Survive
by his most famous project, Los Lobos. Another standout for me, �Navegar� features a slack string guitar solo reminiscent of Duane Eddie and one of many tasty lap steel turns by Sonny Lim. Their interpretation of Woody Guthrie's �Deportee� moves into social commentary, highlighting the cruel realities of being a migrant worker in America.
Vaquero Paniolo
Recorded over five days, mostly live in one room at the Los Cenzontles headquarters in San Pablo, California, including the talents of some of their academy�s students, the recording has real spontaneity to it. Arrangements are stretched by improvisations, sometimes by several different instruments on a single tune. The project also represents a great spirit of cooperation and diversity of language, culture, age, and gender. It includes the inputs of musical legends, seasoned pros, and amateurs. The wonderfully rich and often stereotyped musical cultures of both Mexico and Hawaii are represented here with the authenticity of lived experience.
Adios Ke Aloha: Waves of the Same Sea
is a worthy addition to Los Cenzontles� important work. Quoting Rodriguez again, �Culture is a fabric within which we are all woven.�

items.body:
Live at Rockpalast 1999
documents a command performance at the Loreley open-air amphitheater by Malcolm �Mac� Rebennack Jr., aka Dr. John. Rockpalast is a live-music TV show broadcast since 1974 by Westdeutscher Rundfunk (WDR), the archival source for this CD-DVD package, and coincidentally a remarkable cultural institution on its own terms.
Taped at the height of Dr. John�s international popularity, backing the singer-pianist-guitarist are New Orleans stalwarts Bobby Broom (guitar), David Barard (bass), and Herman Ernest (drums), a tight quartet that projects authority and engages the crowd from start to close.
A striking UNESCO-designated World Heritage Site set, the Loreley is a slate pinnacle on a mythic horseshoe bend of the Rhine River, memorializing an enduring German literary legend both tragic and romantic. The setting is thus well-suited for Mac�s mystical spirit and lyrical style. By this stage of his career, he characterized his live show as a Mardi Gras revue with a mix of New Orleans standards and some of his most recognizable compositions.
Hence, he opens with the NOLA classic �Iko, Iko,� a half-sung, half-chanted celebration of community participation in the renowned Mardi Gras second-line street procession. Then comes the in-your-face boast �Qualified,� wherein the singer warns, �I got the power to control / I can see clean through you, blind mole / I want to tell you now, I'm qualified / You know that I'm qualified.�
Any Dr. John fan will recognize �I Walk on Guilded Splinters,� a moody, percussively insistent, foreboding expression of the Night Tripper�s immersion in �funknology� (his term), gris-gris herbology, and hoodoo incantation, punctuated with jungle growls and cries, a loopy, spooky slide whistle, and an extended psych-guitar solo: �Walk thru the fire / Fly thru the smoke / See my enemy / At the end of dey rope.�
Every piece in this well- honed set deserves considertion. Although Dr John lived for many years in Los Angeles and New York, his enduring hometown connection shows in the fond inclusion of his own �Sweet Home New Orleans� and �Goin� Back to New Orleans,� and he nods to a key influence with a funky rendering of Duke Ellington�s �I'm Gonna Go Fishin�.� Among other gems are Mac�s Top�10 hit �Right Place, Wrong Time,� and the instantly recognizable closer, Earl King�s �Big Chief,� another Mardi Gras burner.
Regarding his live performance approach, per the notes, �I always play a little bit of everything. I think that�s what music�s about: a little bit of somethin� old, somethin� in the middle, somethin� new, and somethin� as yet uncreated.�
Dr John's�s longtime fans will welcome this archival gem, which also is a solid introduction for any late comers to the party. Surmounting the barriers of language and culture, the power of
At the Rockpalast
is also evident in the enthusiastic audience response. As he declares, �If you�re gonna get off on somethin� you don�t need to know nothin� about it. Music is a universal language.�

items.body: Review by Abrasmatheus — Crime of the Century is an album that manages to balance the accessibility of pop rock with elements of greater musical complexity. Although it is often associated with Progressive Rock, I see it more as a progressive pop rock album, using progressive elements without fully committing to the more complex characteristics of the genre. This is especially evident in tracks such as "School" and "Rudy", which feature more elaborate structures and development.One of the album's greatest strengths is precisely this balance between melody and sophistication. The songs are quite accessible, but they never feel simplistic. There is clearly a lot of attention to arrangements, dynamics and development, allowing the album to work both as a collection of great melodies and as a record with plenty of interesting musical details.Among the tracks, "School" is one of the major highlights, with an excellent combination of atmosphere, instrumentation and development. "Hide in Your Shell" is also one of my favorites and, in particular, one of the tracks that best represents what I find special about this album. "Bloody Well Right" and "Asylum" are also excellent, while "Dreamer", despite being a very good song, takes a more direct and accessible approach.The instrumentation is another strong point. The saxophone is particularly distinctive and contributes greatly to the album's identity. The keyboards also play an important role, although I find the saxophone more impressive overall. The drums are very well played, while the guitar and bass are effective without necessarily being the instruments that stand out the most.But the biggest vocal highlight is undoubtedly Roger Hodgson. His voice has a very distinctive character and is immediately recognizable. His high register and particular way of delivering melodies give Supertramp an identity that I find difficult to compare with other bands. The vocal melodies are excellent and are probably among the strongest aspects of the entire album. Rick Davies also delivers very good vocals, but Hodgson's voice is more memorable to me.The production has aged extremely well. The mixing is excellent, and the instruments are very clearly defined, allowing each element to be heard without difficulty. The album has a very balanced sound and still works remarkably well decades after its release. A particularly interesting production moment is the final section of "Asylum", which creates a very engaging atmosphere.I also consider the themes of the album to be important. There is a predominantly melancholic atmosphere connected to the human and social issues addressed throughout the songs. Subjects such as education, isolation and other recurring social problems appear in different forms. The title Crime of the Century itself can be interpreted as a criticism of the problems created by society and the kind of prison that society can impose on individuals.The cover reinforces this idea very effectively. The image of what appears to be a prison fits the atmosphere of the album and can be interpreted as a symbolic representation of society and the limitations it imposes. It is a cover that I consider extremely appropriate for the album's content.Despite its qualities, I do not consider Crime of the Century one of the greatest examples of Progressive Rock in the strictest sense of the genre. Its historical importance is significant, but I believe there are many albums that are much more progressive and representative of the genre. For this reason, I would not necessarily recommend it as an introduction to Progressive Rock. It can work very well as a bridge between rock/pop and progressive music, but there are bands with much more complex approaches and much stronger connections to the genre.I also do not consider the album particularly innovative in terms of progressive music, although it contains some interesting ideas and has a very strong individual identity. In fact, one of the most difficult things about it is finding other bands to compare it with, since Supertramp has a very distinctive sound of its own.Among its strongest points are the very well-defined instrumentation, especially the saxophone and keyboards, Roger Hodgson's vocals, and the themes behind the songs. I do not see many significant weaknesses in the album. My main reservation concerns the final tracks: although they are good, I find the first part of the album stronger and more memorable. "Crime of the Century", the title track, is the song that impresses me the least, although I still consider it a good composition.Overall, I consider Crime of the Century a very good album, with an excellent balance between accessibility, strong melodies, sophisticated instrumentation, distinctive vocals and social themes. The opening tracks, especially "School" and "Hide in Your Shell", are among its greatest highlights, and the production remains impressive.It is not, for me, an essential Progressive Rock album in the strictest sense of the genre, but it is a high-quality record with a very strong identity. Its ability to naturally combine pop rock with progressive elements is precisely what makes it special.

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑在流行摇滚的可听性与渐进摇滚的复杂性之间寻求平衡，被作者定位为'渐进流行摇滚'而非纯粹的先锋作品。歌曲结构较为精致，旋律鲜明，编曲注重层次与动态发展，萨克斯管的运用尤为突出，成为乐队的标志性声音。Roger Hodgson的高音域人声具有极强的辨识度，键盘、鼓与贝斯共同构建了层次分明的音场。制作精良，混音清晰，历经数十年依然耐听。主题聚焦于教育、孤独与社会批判等议题，封面设计亦呼应了这一批判视角。整体而言，这是一张在旋律性与精致度之间取得良好平衡的专辑，但并未深入实验、前卫或爵士领域，对追求极端实验或即兴探索的听众而言，跨界空间有限。

items.excerpt: Review by Hector Enrique — The progressive metal movement, whose foundations were first laid in the mid-to-late 1980s by pioneers such as Queensr�che, Fates Warning, and Dream Theater, gained a much stronger identity and momentum during the 1990s, eventually expanding and establishing itself as a fully-fledged genre in the 2000s. Redemption belongs to the group of bands that emerged under that inspiring influence, shaping a powerful and virtuosic musical approach, immersed in the intricate
items.body: Review by Hector Enrique — The progressive metal movement, whose foundations were first laid in the mid-to-late 1980s by pioneers such as Queensr�che, Fates Warning, and Dream Theater, gained a much stronger identity and momentum during the 1990s, eventually expanding and establishing itself as a fully-fledged genre in the 2000s. Redemption belongs to the group of bands that emerged under that inspiring influence, shaping a powerful and virtuosic musical approach, immersed in the intricate structures of the most contemporary prog metal.With their self-titled 2003 debut album, Redemption had already shown what they were capable of, although it was still a somewhat raw and unpolished power-metal-style offering with nascent progressive elements. For "The Fullness of Time" (2005), their second album, the band led by Nick van Dyk brought in the duo James Sherwood (bass) and Chris Quirarte (drums), both from the ranks of the Los Angeles-based band Prymary, as their new rhythm section, and, most importantly, vocalist Ray Alder -who also fronted Fates Warning- evolving toward a more defined and mature sound.The first third of the album retains the band's seminal sound, with machine-gun-like, galloping riffs; frenzied, counterpointing solos between Bernie Versailles and van Dyk; and Quirarte's wild double-bass drumming, to which van Dyk's keyboards add an additional, fitting melodic and atmospheric layer, both on the aggressive "Threads," the fast-paced "Scarred," and the reflective and bitter "Parker's Eyes" -which offers a somber and disheartening view of the world, including a reference to the events of 9/11- and incorporates a beautiful, arpeggiated acoustic nuance before exploding instrumentally.The following two-thirds reflect the band's solidity and progressive character, with the epic "Sapphire", a powerful and expansive instrumental tapestry led by a spirited Alder on vocals and generous with guitar and synthesizer solos, contrasted with calm, refreshing passages -the jewel of the album- and the intricate "The Fullness of Time," a suite divided into four sections where journeys through rocky peaks -the furious and vengeful "i. Rage" and the resilient "iii. Release"- alternate with clear, evocative sonic valleys -the meditative "ii. Despair" and the hopeful and luminous "iv. Trascendence"."The Fullness of Time" marked a turning point in Redemption's career: an album in which the band left behind the rough edges of its debut to find its own identity, delivering one of the genre's strongest offerings of the mid-2000s.4/4.5 stars
items._genre: progressive metal / power metal / heavy metal
items._cn_summary: Redemption的第二张专辑《The Fullness of Time》延续了九十年代前卫金属的传统血脉，受Queensrÿche、Fates Warning、Dream Theater等先驱影响。乐队在引入Fates Warning主唱Ray Alder以及新节奏组合后，从首张专辑较为粗糙的力量金属雏形中蜕变出来，确立了更成熟的方向。专辑前段以密集连复段、双底鼓冲击和双吉他对位独奏见长，收录了反映9/11事件氛围的苦涩之作。后三分之二走向更典型的前卫金属路线，包括器乐色彩浓郁的史诗长曲和分为四个乐章的标题组曲，在暴烈段落与冥想性段落之间交替推进。评论将此作视为乐队找到自身定位的转折点，也是该流派中期内最具分量的作品之一。

items.body: Review by UMUR — "Section X" is the second full-length studio album by Danish power/progressive metal act BeyondTwilight (if you discount the two Twilight albums as the works of another band). The album wasreleased through Massacre Records in March 2005. It�s the successor to "The Devil's Hall of Fame"from 2001. The nucleus of the band is intact (namely keyboard player and band founder Finn Zierler,guitarist Anders Ericson Kragh, bassist Anders Lindgren, and drummer Tomas Fred�n) since the releaseof "The Devil's Hall of Fame" but there have been a couple of lineup changes. The omnipresent JacobHansen (Invocator, Anubis Gate, Pyramaze...etc.) has joined on guitars and vocals, and American leadvocalist Kelly Sundown Carpenter (Darkology, Inner Sanctum, Outworld...etc.) has replaced Norwegianvocalist J�rn Lande (Ark, Masterplan, Allen - Lande...etc.).Stylistically the material on "Section X" is a combination of epic power metal and heavy metaloriented progressive metal. The latter means that this is progressive oriented music but nottechnical for the sake of it, and you shouldn't expect long instrumental sections dominating thetracks. Beyond Twilight�s music is more song oriented and generally features relatively accessibleverse/chorus structures. The tracks are quite sophisticated though (listen to the almost theatrical"Sleeping Beauty"). The closest relative is to my ears Symphony X because of the power metal andprogressive metal hybrid style, but also because of the epic nature of the music, the heaviness ofthe music (this is not vanilla Euro power metal), and the omnipresence of keyboards. Carpenter isquite the impressive singer with a strong voice and commanding delivery and the musicianship isgenerally through the roof on this release."Section X" features a powerful, heavy, and detailed sound production. It�s polished and wellproduced but still heavy and raw enough not to become too sterile sounding. Every instrument andvocal part stand out in the mix and are perfectly balanced. Just because this is Zierler�s projectdoesn�t mean that the keyboards overshadow everything else. On the contrary Zierler is veryconscious in terms of when his keyboards should dominate a track and when they shouldn�t. Uponconclusion "Section X" is a step up in quality from the already great "The Devil's Hall of Fame" andit�s just through and through a high quality release from Beyond Twilight. A 4 - 4.5 star (85%)rating is deserved.(Originally posted on Metal Music Archives).

items._cn_summary: Beyond Twilight 是丹麦力量前卫金属乐队，《Section X》是其第二张全长专辑，由 Massacre Records 于2005年发行。乐队核心由键盘手兼创始人 Finn Zierler 领衔，阵容历经变动后由 Jacob Hansen 兼任吉他和声部，美国主唱 Kelly Sundown Carpenter 接替挪威歌手 Jørn Lande 担任主唱。音乐融合史诗力量金属与重金属取向的前卫金属，注重歌曲结构而非炫技式器乐段落，但编曲相当精致，部分曲目如《Sleeping Beauty》呈现出近乎戏剧化的风格。评论将其与 Symphony X 类比，强调键盘的贯穿作用与整体厚重感。制作方面，音墙饱满且层次清晰，各乐器与人声平衡得当，乐评人给予约 85% 的高分评价，视为前作《The Devil's Hall of Fame》的品质升级。然而该风格属于传统金属范畴内的常规演变，与实验、前卫爵士、电子或暗潮等领域的交集有限。

items.body: Kontravoid released his new album “Sound Of The Void” on 2 October 2026 via Artoffact Records. The ten-track release is Cameron Findlay’s second full-length for the Toronto label, following 2024’s “Detachment.” Coldwave, EBM and electro run through the record. Side-Line covered the album’s announcement in September, when “Without” arrived as the first advance track. “Mortal” and “Chances” followed ahead of the full release. Sound Of The Void by Kontravoid The tracklist runs “Sound Of The Void,” “Without,” “Mortal,” “Subject,” “Chances,” “Dimension,” “Forever,” “Abandon,” “Returning” and “Phantom.” “Sound Of The Void” is available digitally and on CD, with a clear-vinyl first pressing also available on Bandcamp. About Kontravoid Kontravoid is the solo project of Canadian musician and producer Cameron Findlay, now based in Los Angeles. Before starting Kontravoid, he played drums with Crystal Castles in 2007 and 2008 and was a founding member of Toronto synth-pop band Parallels. His self-titled Kontravoid debut followed in 2012, released through the Minimal Wave label. He has toured North America alongside Buzz Kull, and the mask he wears on stage has become part of the project’s identity, a presence carried into “Sound Of The Void.”

items.body:
The musical partnership between Kalaniemi and Alakotila has thrived over a remarkable 35 years, long enough to the Finnish pair to develop a stunning intimacy and telepathy. Kalaniemi is a lovingly melodic accordion player, with a sharp ear for a good tune, building each one into a thing of great beauty, while pianist Alakotila not only supports her but adds enough of his own to help transform every piece into a glistening gem.
There�s a sense of calmness to the work here, a long, sweet exhalation between two instrumentalists who are deep enough in sync to allow seamless improvisation beyond any written score and carry the listeners along with them. For much of the album, it�s just the pair of them, including Kalaniemi�s wordless voice, as on the opener, the tradional �Lyck�nskan.� She does charmingly sing lyrics on the title track, written by Lasse M�rtenson, with the sound there neatly and sparingly expanded with the addition of a string quartet.
Morgondimma
There are several original pieces alongside the tradition, with Kalaniemi�s �Hambo Vid F�bodan� a real standout, and it�s perhaps inevitable on any disc featuring accordion that a Piazzolla tune should be included, brings its own shadows to the whole (�Oblivion�). And, this being Finland, a tango is almost obligatory, in this case Alakotila�s �Tango Berlin.�
Tango Berlin
There�s a gentle, dreamlike quality to so much of this, flowing and mellifluous. The pieces aren�t an arena for showy virtuosity. Instead, the two musicians serve the tune, exploring and genuinely enjoying their performances.
It won�t shake the earth, but it makes for some true listening beauty.

items.body:
Sometime in 1986, perhaps in a Paris caf�, Dominique Cravic, a singer, guitarist, and musical archivist, met Robert Crumb, an underground cartoonist, banjo and mandolin player, and jug-band aficionado. Over a few glasses of marc, to continue to speculate, they conjured up the idea for Les Primitifs du futur.  Since then, they have recorded an impossible-to-categorize series of albums, with cover illustrations by Crumb, of which Les Crimes du Mussette is the fifth.
Weird and wonderful, it sounds like they rooted through an attic full of 78 RPM records, scribbled down some arrangements, and then played them on a collection of instruments they found in another attic, including accordion, sax, xylophone, clarinet, banjo, ukulele, theremin, Hawaiian guitar, bagpipe chanter (I�m guessing here), and musical saw.
Ne tirez pas sur le pianiste (excerpt)
The 27 short tracks are mostly voiced by Cravic, who talk-sings in the manner of an everyman Maurice Chevalier. He is often accompanied by the accordion, a customary instrument in the bal-musette style that remains a strong element of the eclectic range of styles they have managed to synthesize. They also include ragtime, jug, French chanson, and, to my ears, skiffle,  just to get the list started.
Ukulele Lady (excerpt)
The liner notes point out that �Les Crimes du Musette is also a gold mine for scholars, a veritable treasure trove.� Exploring the treasures is beyond my scope here, as each tune has a long history. A highlight for me is the humorous �Ukulele Lady� from 1925, which first delighted me on Arlo Guthrie�s 1971 album
Hobo�s Lullaby
. The song has also been covered by Bing Crosby, Peter Sellers, and Bette Midler.
N'oublie pas Gr�co (excerpt)
A more serious item is �N�oublie pas Gr�co� (Don�t Forget Gr�co�)  is a tribute to the legendary chanteuse and heroine of the French Resistance, Juliette Gr�co, who died in 2020. You will also hear old chestnuts like �Fum�e aux yeux� (�Smoke Gets in Your Eyes�),  �Boude pas� (�Take Five�), and �Prive d�amour� (�As Time Goes By�).
This record is a curiosity, but it is performed by serious musicians with total commitment. In this, I was reminded of the similarly indefinable Dan Hicks & the Hot Licks. Long-forgotten music and abandoned styles are given new animation with obvious enthusiasm and care. Speaking about himself and his collaborators, many of whom are in their seventies, Dominique Cravic says, �The young have fire, but we have light.� In its own little corner,
Les Crimes du Musette
shines bright.

Vanishment

Genuine Negro Jig

items._cn_summary: 这张专辑是Dominique Cravic与Les Primitifs du futur的第五张作品，源于他1986年与漫画家Robert Crumb的一次咖啡馆相遇。乐队以复古的姿态漫游于多种被遗忘的风格之间：巴黎bal-musette的手风琴传统、拉格泰姆、jug band、法国香颂，甚至带有skiffle气息。27首短曲由Cravic以近似Maurice Chevalier的念白式唱腔演绎，伴奏乐器包括班卓琴、尤克里里、口琴、萨克斯、锯琴、theremin等。曲目多为老歌翻唱，如1925年的《Ukulele Lady》以及向法国抵抗运动歌手Juliette Gréco致敬的《N'oublie pas Gréco》。整张专辑像是从78转唱片匣子里挖掘出的声音档案，由一群七旬上下的音乐家以严肃的态度重新赋予生命。虽然乐评提到其'无法归类'的特质，但其本质更偏向对旧日素材的复古拼贴与致敬，而非真正的前卫实验或创新声音设计。

items.body: Review by martindavey87 — Arguably one of the more radio-friendly hits from Dream Theater's 1994 album, 'Awake', 'Lie' is a groovy, riff-laden rocker that has some fantastic vocals and great instrumentation. After the success of 'Pull Me Under' a couple of years earlier, this track was probably the best choice for appealing to mainstream rock and metal fans, so its choice as a single is more than justified. Additional tracks include the ballads 'Space Dye Vest', which is keyboardist Kevin Moore's hauntingly beautiful swansong with the band, and one of many different recorded versions of 'To Live Forever', a song the band had played live for many years prior to this, but had never gotten around to recording a studio version of. As well as a live recording of 'Another Day', this is a pretty decent CD single for collectors and die-hard fans of the band.

items.body: Review by martindavey87 — Released in 2007 through the bands official fan club, 'Images and Words 15th Anniversary Performance' is literally what it says it is; Dream Theater playing the entire album that forever set the standard for all progressive metal bands to follow. Of course, it has its pros and cons. There's some interesting embellishments dotted around, which could keep us prog nerds at least somewhat invested for a little while, and it's cool to hear Jordan Rudess interpret some of Kevin Moore's keyboard parts. Then of course, there's vocalist James LaBrie. Sure, he struggles with some of it due to age and a well-documented vocal injury, but I guess at least he's trying. The band would go on to release a 25th anniversary performance of this album through their 'Lost Not Forgotten' series many years later, so, you know, it's probably slightly better than that one, again, due to LaBrie being another ten years older by then and struggling even more. Bless him. I don't think I'd ever choose to actually listen to this over the original 1992 studio album, which, for the record, is my favourite album of all time. But the name of this release describes exactly what you're getting here, so there's absolutely no point in taking it too seriously. It's a cool addition to the collection, and if you're a die-hard Dream Theater fan like I am, then you'll enjoy owning it. Simple as that.

items.body: Montreal dark-alternative artist Martin Saint released the single “Endless Bridge” on October 6, 2026, as a standalone digital track on Bandcamp. Martin Saint wrote and arranged “Endless Bridge” himself and handled vocals and guitars. Julie Abel plays piano, Frank Bones plays drums and Jack Vignavong plays bass. The track was recorded at Martini Lounge, Indica Studio 24 and Studio Pacifique in Montreal by Frank Bones and Martin Saint, with assistance from Olivier René de Cotret. Frank Bones mixed and mastered the track and co-produced it with Martin Saint. Ursa Minor handled the sleeve photography and design. Endless Bridge by Martin Saint In the track’s Bandcamp notes, Martin Saint described the song as a love story told through departures and returns. “Endless Bridge is about as close to a love song as I’ll ever get, but there’s a bittersweetness to it. Beginnings, endings, renewals. It expresses faith in the future and letting go of forces holding us back, even if this may take a lifetime.” He pointed to two specific reference points for the track’s sound: “Musically, I wanted something that’d sound as epic as The Killing Moon or With or Without You, for example. Melancholy, foggy, but uplifting and catchy.” “Endless Bridge” is available now as a name-your-price digital download on Bandcamp, with a minimum price of $1.50. About Martin Saint Martin Saint is a solo artist based in Montreal, Québec. Before launching the project under his own name, he was the lead singer and second guitarist of the city’s indie-rock quartet The Ember Glows, active between 2019 and 2024. His solo material moves into darker, more atmospheric territory, with baritone, emotionally-charged vocals and poetic lyrics that he has linked to Bauhaus, The Mission, The Jesus and Mary Chain, Nick Cave, Leonard Cohen and The Doors. “Endless Bridge” follows “Seekers,” Martin Saint’s fifth release under the solo name, out April 18, 2025. The ten-track album was recorded and mixed in Montreal at the Martini Lounge and Orange Studio by Martin Saint and Frank Bones, who also mastered it, with guest contributions from Julie Abel on piano, Delphine Dupont on lead guitar and backing vocals, Kevin Hills on bass, Hugo Joyal on pedal steel and Ursa Minor on backing vocals and artwork. His catalog also includes the albums “One Word Away,” “Fly Tales” and “Radio Murmurs,” along with the singles “Last Lights,” “The Law” and “I’ll Be Your Stranger,” featuring Ursa Minor. “Endless Bridge” carries the same core production team as “Seekers” into a new standalone single.

items.body: これから楽器をはじめる初心者から、ふたたび楽器を手にした再始動プレイヤー、さらには現役バンドマンまで、「もっと上手に、もっと楽しく」演奏したい皆さんに贈るジャムセッション講座シリーズ。 今回訪れたのは、創立70周年を迎えた日本最古のジャズ専門スクール「飯田ジャズスクール」。戦後日本のジャズ黎明期から続くこの場所で体験レッスンに参加したものの……。 【今回の現場】 飯田ジャズスクール 1955年創立、日本最古のジャズ専門スクール。ジャズ黎明期から続く老舗で、ピアノ、サックス、ギター、ベース、ドラム、ボーカルなど幅広いコースを開講している。講師陣には、ピアニストの宮本貴奈、サックス奏者の大山日出男、多田誠司、トランペッターの岡崎好朗ら第一線のミュージシャンが名を連ねる。個人レッスンに加え、固定メンバーによるアンサンブルレッスンを重視しているのが特徴で、初心者からセミプロレベルまで幅広い層が通う。 東京都杉並区下高井戸2-8-4／03-5376-1353 【担当記者】 千駄木雄大（せんだぎ ゆうだい） ライター。32歳。大学時代に軽音楽サークルに所属。基本的なコードとパワーコードしか弾けない。セッションに参加して立派に演奏できるようになるまで、この連載を終えることができないという十字架を背負っている。最近、InstagramでAKAI MPC Sampleの動画がやたら流れてくるので、「買っちゃおうかな」と調べたら、6万円くらいした。プロも使う機材なのだから当然なのだが、それ以来、機材だらけの部屋にいる人のInstagram投稿を見るたびに、「この人たち、いったい楽器にいくら注ぎ込んでるんだ……」と震えるようになった。 フリーライター、ジャムセッションへ行けない この連載が始まって4年目。一向にジャムセッションに参加していない。それもそのはずだ。曲の練習はしているものの、圧倒的に練習量が足りていないからだ。 働き盛りの32歳。フリーランスという働き方ゆえ、毎日牛のように働かなければ、生活していくための日銭も得られない。それに、いくら稼げるといっても、税金や福利厚生などを考えると、フリーランスは正社員の1.5倍は働かなければならないという現実もある。 筆者には嫁も子もいないが、妹夫婦の子育てを見ていると、ひとりで生きるだけでも毎日バタバタして時間がないのに、子どもを寝かしつけるとなれば、もう自由な時間などなさそうだ。 そう考えると、楽器演奏というのは贅沢な趣味である。お金にはならないが、好きな曲を弾いて、YouTubeに“弾いてみた動画”として記録を残すこともできる。そして、そんな趣味を持つ者同士が集まってバンドを組み、演奏するとなると、お金と時間に余裕がなければ難しい。 長々とよくわからないことを書いてきたが、要するに、4年も経っているのにジャムセッションに参加できるレベルにまったく達していないということだ。さすがに「枯葉」など2〜3曲は弾けるようになったが、いまだにギターのどこを押さえれば「ドレミ」と鳴るのかがよくわからない。そもそも、「ドレミ」ってどんな音だ？ もちろん、20年近くギターを触っているだけあって、感覚的にどこを押さえれば考えている音が鳴るかは把握している。ただ、コードトーンなどを理解せず闇雲に弾いていると、手は動いても頭では何も考えていないため、技術の向上にはつながらない。 YouTubeでジャズブルースの伴奏を流し、それっぽくアドリブを弾いて、「なんかよくできたかも」と思う。だが、録音した自分の演奏を聴き直すと、音程も音量も何もかもが合っておらず、聴いていられない。 「これは自分だけではどうにもならないな」 専門家に習ったほうが、理論などの疑問もひとりで抱え込まずに済むし、上達も早そうだ。そうだ、スクールに通おう！ せっかくなら、本格的な講師に習ってみたい。もしかしたら、編集部に頼めば月謝を払ってくれるかもしれない……。 ということで、日本で最初に誕生したジャズ専門の学校「飯田ジャズスクール」の無料見学＆体験レッスンに応募。すると、「ぜひアンサンブルの日にお越しください」と快諾された。 あれ……。なんだか急にハイレベルな話になってきたぞ。 日本最古のジャズスクールが生まれた歴史的背景 杉並区下高井戸の住宅街（桜上水駅）。マンション１階の地下へ降りると、サックスの音が漏れてくる。ドラムがテンポを刻み、ピアノが応える。 「あっ、千駄木さんですね。お待ちしておりましたよ」 そう語りかけてきたのは、ギタリストの松井洋氏。この日は同氏をバンドマスターとして、アンサンブル演奏が行われていた。 創立70年を迎えた飯田ジャズスクールは、日本のジャズ史そのものと重なるような歴史を持っている。同校の始まりは、現在の杉並区下高井戸ではなく、杉並区方南町だった。 創設者は飯田龍夫氏。1954年、ジャズベースの教則本『ベース教本』を出版している。 「当時は、ジャズの教則本なんてほとんどなかったんですよ」 そう語るのは、龍夫氏の息子であり、学院長を務める飯田敏彦氏。そもそも、当時のジャズは今とは役割が違った。 「米軍もいて、クラブやキャバレーがたくさんあった時代です。だから、演奏する側も “芸術としてのジャズ” というより、ダンスミュージックとして演奏していました。今みたいに、アマチュアがジャムセッションをやる場所はほとんどなく、みんな“仕事” として演奏していた時代です」 スクールへ通う生徒たちも、「ジャズが好きだから」ではなく、「演奏で食べていきたい」という目的を持つ人が多かった。 しかし、戦後の日本では、「ジャズを学ぶ」という文化自体がほとんど存在していなかった。ピアノやクラシックの教本はあっても、「ジャズ」と銘打った教材は極めて少ない。ましてや、ベースの教則本はほぼ皆無だった。 「そんな中、父はウッドベースの教則本を書いたんです。そして、本の読者たちが『この著者に習いたい』ということで、父のもとを訪れるようになった。それが、飯田ジャズスクールの始まりです」 創設者の飯田龍夫氏（右）と息子で現学院長を務める飯田敏彦氏（左） クラブやキャバレーが多く存在した当時は、演奏者としてそこで働くほうが、サラリーマンよりもはるかに給料が良かった。それに、固定給でもある。 「つまり、ジャズという音楽の日本での捉えられ方が、今とはまったく違ったわけです。そこから、秋吉敏子さんや渡辺貞夫さんなど、海外プレイヤーに引けを取らない日本人ミュージシャンたちが登場し、ジャズが社会全体に広がっていきます。そして、プロにならなくても、普通の仕事をしながら趣味で音楽をやる人たちが増えてきた。そういう人たちがうちに来て習い、弾けるようになると、今度はアンサンブルに興味が出てくるのです」 “趣味のジャズ”を支えるアンサンブル文化 現在、飯田ジャズスクールの生徒数は約160人。 「昔はプロ志向の学生が多かったですが、今はうちに通わなくても、国立音楽大学や洗足学園音楽大学のようにジャズ科がある音大へ進学する人が増えました」 代わりに増えたのが、「仕事ではなく趣味としてのジャズをやりたい」という社会人たちだ。平日は会社員として働き、休日になるとサックスやピアノを持ってスクールへやってくる。 「“趣味だからこれくらいできればいい”とは、誰も思っていません。みなさん、真剣に上達したいという気持ちで通っています」 同スクールの特徴は、アンサンブル重視のレッスンにある。現在、15〜20組ほどの固定バンドが存在し、生徒が辞める場合もあるが、基本的には同じメンバーで継続的に演奏を重ねている。 ジャムセッションでは、その場限りのメンバーによる即興演奏が中心だ。しかし、アンサンブルでは「来月はこの曲をやりましょう」と事前に決め、メンバー全員が練習してくる。 「ジャムセッションと違って、ある程度固定されたメンバーで、自分のバンドのような感覚で演奏できます。そして、毎回同じメンバーだから、一体感も生まれる。曲を繰り返し演奏することで、どんどんレベルも上がっていきます」 当然、メンバー構成にも気を遣う。ドラムやベースは生徒数が少ないだけではなく、リズム隊としての安定感も求められる。それに、経験差が大きすぎれば、バンド全体が崩れてしまう。 そのため、敏彦氏は生徒一人ひとりの性格や技量を見ながら、アンサンブルの編成を調整している。 「うちには個人レッスンの生徒さんがたくさんいて、上達していくと、『ひとりでやるよりバンドで演奏したい』という話になるんです。そこで先生が、『君だったらアンサンブルに入れるよ』と判断するわけです。逆に、『もう少し個人レッスンをしたほうがいい』という場合は、無理に入れることはありません。適当にメンバーを組み合わせても、うまくいかないんですよ。相性もありますし、協調性も必要です」 レッスンはだいたい月２回。個人レッスンを受けながら、アンサンブルにも参加している生徒もいる。アンサンブルだけに参加する生徒もいるが、ある程度のレベルが必要だ。 「3年くらい個人レッスンとアンサンブルを両方やっていて、『だいぶ上手くなったので、個人レッスンはやめてアンサンブルだけにします』という生徒もいます。レベルに合わせて、いろいろ選べます」 30年通う生徒も！ アンサンブルが“居場所”になる理由 飯田ジャズスクールには、30年以上通い続けている生徒がいる。しかも、ひとりやふたりではない。5〜6人ほどが、ほぼ人生の半分に近い時間をこの場所で過ごしてきたという。 「習うというより、ずっとアンサンブルを続けている感じですね」 単に “ジャズを習う場” というだけではないのが、このスクールの特徴でもある。また、アンサンブルクラスにも明確なレベル分けが存在する。 「たとえば松井先生のクラスは、“アンサンブルをあまりやったことがない人” でも受け入れるんです。もちろん、最低限の演奏力は必要になりますが、『少しアドリブができる』程度からでも参加可能です。一方で、上級クラスになると空気は一変して、かなりビバップ中心になりますね。そこまで行くと、もうセミプロと言っても過言ではない」 技術だけではなく、“ジャズの空気” そのものが変わる。厳しい指導を求め、自らその環境へ飛び込んでくる生徒も少なくない。 「別に怒鳴るわけじゃないんです。でも、その空気を求めて皆さん来ている。そこを甘くすると、逆に満足しないんですよ。それに、うちは学校ではなく、ジャズスクール。大学のように4年で卒業するわけではないため、続けるのも自由だし、辞めるのも自由。本当に本人次第なんです」   もちろん、生徒たちは外部のジャムセッションへ足を運ぶこともある。しかし、即席メンバーでの演奏に満足感を覚えず、結局この場所でのアンサンブルが性に合っていると実感するのだという。 また、飯田ジャズスクールには、「長く通うほど安くなる」といった制度はない。月謝制で、基本的には１カ月ごとの支払いだ。 「無理やり『１年分払ってください』ということはしません。だからこそ、続けるかどうかは完全に本人次第になる。上手くなるかどうかも本人なんです」 一方で、スクール側は “環境”は整える。初心者を丁寧に見る講師もいれば、ハイレベルなビバップを徹底的に鍛える講師もいる。その器を維持し続けることこそが、70年近くスクールを続けてきた理由なのだろう。 そして今後は、その役割を娘の飯田さつき氏へ引き継いでいくという。 「今はヴォーカル講師として生徒たちに接していますが、これからは娘が、アンサンブルの組み合わせなどもやっていくことになると思います。アンサンブル編成は、おはじきのように適当に組めばいいものではない。生徒の性格や希望を細かく見る必要があります」 ライオンの檻に放り込まれたうさぎの末路 そして今回、筆者が無料見学と体験レッスンに参加したのは、結成から２年ほど活動を続けているアンサンブルグループだった。いや、さすがにレベルが高すぎる。 「さあ、『枯葉』でもブルースでも、好きな曲をやりましょう。リクエストしてください」 松井氏は笑顔でそう促してくれる。しかし、こちらはそのレベルに届いていないからこそ、教わりに来たのだ。 とはいえ、いつまでも言い訳ばかりしているわけにはいかない。噴き出す冷や汗を拭いながらギターを取り出し、アンプにつなぐ。そして小さな声で、「『枯葉』なら弾けます」と伝えた。 本当はコード進行をなんとなく覚えているだけで、アドリブも雰囲気でごまかしているに過ぎない。 いざ、演奏が始まると、今度は自分のギターの音がほとんど聞こえなかった。演奏力のなさを隠そうとして音量を下げていたのだから当然だ。しかも極度に緊張していたせいで、うまく弾けず、コードをかき鳴らすだけでも音が濁ってしまう。情けなさでいっぱいになった。 メンバーたちは気を遣ってソロパートも回してくれたが、結局テーマをなぞるだけで精一杯。演奏はあっという間に終わり、松井氏たちは温かい言葉をかけてくれたものの、恥ずかしさに耐えきれず、その場を早々に後にした。本当に申し訳ない気持ちだった。 帰り際、一連の出来事を飯田氏に話すと、穏やかな口調でこう語ってくれた。 「ジャズは “敷居が高い音楽” だと思われがちですよね。でも、最初からできる人なんていません。ちゃんと順番に経験を積めばいいんですよ。今日だって、みなさん優しかったでしょう？ もし怒ってばかりいたら、誰も来なくなってしまいます（笑）」 さらにこう続ける。 「ジャズは、“間違えてはいけない音楽” ではありません。間違えたあとに、どう立て直すかを楽しむ音楽なんです。失敗しても終わりじゃない。そこから戻ればいいし、周りも支えてくれる。ひとりだけが上手ければ成立するものでもありません。互いの音を聴きながら、みんなで音楽を作っていく。その面白さが、ジャズにはあるんです」 次こそは、納得できる演奏をしたい……。そう思いながら、筆者はノートパソコンの横に静かに置かれたギターを眺めていた。 ARBAN に最初に表示されました。

items._cn_summary: 本文并非传统意义上的音乐评论或专辑评介，而是一篇连载性质的教学体验报道。记者以初学者视角走访创立于1955年的飯田ジャズスクール，参与其Ensemble课程体验。文中穿插该学院的历史沿革——从战后美军俱乐部驻场演奏时代，到如今以业余爱好者为主的教学模式转变，并介绍了学院长飯田敏彦及客座讲师阵容。文章涉及日本爵士教育史的背景叙述，但整体内容偏向生活随笔与求学体验，缺乏对具体音乐技法、演奏分析或声音设计的深入探讨。

items.body:
Clockenflap has unveiled its first wave of artists for 2026, with Hayley Williams, keshi, Slowdive, and Queens of the Stone Age among the names heading to Hong Kong.

The music and arts festival returns to Central Harbourfront Event Space from 4 to 6 December, bringing three days of live music, art, and activities to the city’s waterfront.

keshi will headline Friday, while Paramore frontwoman Hayley Williams takes the Saturday headline slot with her solo show. Slowdive are confirmed to perform on Sunday.

The first announcement also features alternative R&B artist Malcolm Todd, South Korean indie favourites HYUKOH, Scottish alternative rock outfit The Jesus and Mary Chain, and Sonic Youth co-founder Kim Gordon.

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by Clockenflap (@clockenflap)

Elsewhere on the bill, DOMi & JD BECK and Bre kky Boy bring jazz explorations, while Digable Planets represent alternative hip-hop and Sleaford Mods deliver their distinctive post-punk sound. Electronic music fans can catch Marcel Dettmann and HE.R Soundsystem.

Also joining the line-up are singer-songwriter Daniela Andrade, New Zealand band SIX60, Thai artist pami, dream-pop act Fazerdaze, and genre-blending trio Chanpan.

Beyond its multiple music stages, Clockenflap will feature art installations, family-friendly workshops and performances, and food and drink from Hong Kong outlets, all set against the harbour and city skyline.

General ticket sales begin on 10 October at 3 PM HKT via Ticketflap. Ticket options are:

General admission, three-day weekend: HK$2,180

General admission, single day: HK$1,380

Under-18 admission, three-day weekend: HK$1,680

Under-18 admission, single day: HK$980

Eligible American Express cardmembers can access priority booking with 15% off tickets until 10 October at 2:59 PM HKT. They can subsequently enjoy 12% off tickets from the start of general sales until 10 November at 2:59 PM HKT, subject to terms and availability.

Like what you read? Show our writer some love!

items.body:
JJ Lin, The Killers and Lana Del Rey headline this year’s Formula 1 Singapore Airlines Singapore Grand Prix, but there’s plenty more music to explore across the circuit. Taking place from 9 to 11 October at the Marina Bay Street Circuit, the race weekend also brings together Indonesian indie pop, Japanese guitar rock, British jazz and home-grown favourites.

Whether you’re after an afternoon dance session or a band to add to your daily rotation, here are eight acts worth making time for between the racing action and headline sets.

Coldiac

When: 9 October, 9.30PM to 10.15PM

Where: DBS Foundation Outdoor Theatre at Esplanade, Zone 4

For fans of: Indie pop, R&B and synth-pop

Indonesian trio Coldiac make an appealing case for staying out a little longer. Their music brings together pop hooks, R&B influences and synths, offering plenty for listeners who like their indie pop with a groove.

Tracks such as ‘Wreck This Journal’ and ‘TARA’ helped introduce the band, whose catalogue has since expanded to include Lemons Made Lemonade and singles ‘Eksplorasi’ and ‘Jangan Pernah Berubah’. Their 2025 EP Loving You Like This also sees them put their own spin on Indonesian classics. For newcomers, that mix of original material and reinterpretations offers several routes into their sound ahead of Friday’s set.

KIKI

When: 10 October, 6PM to 6.45PM

Where: DBS Foundation Outdoor Theatre at Esplanade, Zone 4

For fans of: Synth-pop, nu-disco and dreamy dance music

Bangkok trio KIKI make music for anyone who likes a little introspection with their dancing. Their sound moves between guitar pop, funk, nu-disco and electronic textures, pairing reflective songwriting with rhythms that keep things moving.

Singapore listeners may recognise them from Baybeats, while their festival appearances also include Japan’s Fuji Rock and France’s Les Escales. Get acquainted through Post Existential Crisis or Death of a Daisy & Birth of an Oyster, then check out this year’s ‘Wait a Minute’. Their Saturday evening slot makes them a tempting stop for fans looking to explore Thailand’s indie scene.

Ezra Collective

When: 10 October, 3.45PM to 4.30PM

Where: Downtown, Zone 4

For fans of: Jazz, Afrobeat, hip-hop and a proper dance session

Bring your dancing shoes for Ezra Collective. The British quintet’s music draws jazz, Afrobeat, hip-hop and soul into performances built around rhythm and collective movement. Their album Where I’m Meant To Be earned them the Mercury Prize, and they bring that expansive sound to an early Saturday set.

Dance, No One’s Watching is a particularly good introduction to their approach. Try ‘God Gave Me Feet for Dancing’ and ‘Ajala’ before heading down. Drummer Femi Koleoso has spoken about shaping the band’s music around the momentum of a dance floor, and that spirit carries into their live shows, where getting the audience involved is central to the experience. Arrive ready to move.

Pleasantry

When: 10 October, 4PM to 4.45PM

Where: DBS Foundation Outdoor Theatre at Esplanade, Zone 4

For fans of: Dreamy indie music and intricate guitars

Singapore indie favourites Pleasantry reward those who listen closely. The quintet’s appeal lies in the interplay: guitars winding around each other, shifting rhythmic patterns and warm melodies that give their intricate arrangements an inviting centre.

Since Synapses, they’ve remained active on the gig circuit, taking their music overseas and letting songs evolve through years of performances. Their 2025 album Slow Burn captures that patient approach, but the real draw here is catching those musical conversations onstage. Try ‘Constellation’ and ‘Quiet’ before heading down, then listen for how the individual parts come together.

Lola Amour

When: 11 October, 4.30PM to 5.15PM

Where: DBS Foundation Outdoor Theatre at Esplanade, Zone 4

For fans of: Funk-pop, Filipino indie and communal singalongs

You may already know ‘Raining in Manila’. Sunday is your chance to get better acquainted with Lola Amour, the Manila band behind it and fellow favourite ‘Fallen’. Their mix of pop, funk and rock makes them an accessible starting point for anyone looking to explore contemporary Filipino music.

There’s plenty of evidence that their songs come into their own with a crowd. At shows previously covered by Bandwagon, fans have sung back lyrics, joined in with ad-libs and jumped through instrumental breaks. ‘Raining in Manila’ even brought the band onstage with Chris Martin during Coldplay’s Philippine visit in 2024. Come with the chorus learnt, and leave with a few more songs to look up.

TOKiMONSTA

When: 9 October, 3.15PM to 4.15PM

Where: Barge Stage, Zone 1

For fans of: Electronic music, R&B and adventurous production

TOKiMONSTA gives Zone 1 ticketholders a reason to arrive early on Friday. The GRAMMY-nominated producer’s catalogue stretches from Midnight Menu to Eternal Reverie, bringing electronic experimentation into conversation with R&B and a wide range of collaborators, including Anderson .Paak, Yuna and ZHU.

For a taste of that range, start with Eternal Reverie. Its tracks move through disco-pop, soul and quieter instrumental passages, with ‘Lucky U’ and ‘On Sum’ offering two very different entry points. That breadth makes her an intriguing pick for listeners who enjoy following a producer across genres.

Polkadot Stingray

When: 11 October, 6.45PM to 7.30PM

Where: DBS Foundation Outdoor Theatre at Esplanade, Zone 4

For fans of: Japanese rock and nimble guitar work

If guitar bands are your priority, put Polkadot Stingray on your list. Led by vocalist and guitarist Shizuku, the Japanese quartet have built their identity around tightly arranged rock songs, sharp guitar work and an assertive stage presence.

‘Telecaster Stripe’ and ‘Electric Public’ are useful starting points before their Sunday appearance. Shizuku also takes a central role in the band’s songwriting, design and video production, giving listeners a whole visual world to explore alongside the music. At the circuit, though, the draw is straightforward: a chance to hear those intricate arrangements delivered live.

Momocurly

When: 9 October, 5.45PM to 6.30PM

Where: DBS Foundation Outdoor Theatre at Esplanade, Zone 4

For fans of: City pop, jazz and atmospheric indie

For a discovery that might take you somewhere unexpected, try Momocurly. The Tokyo-based French-Japanese duo bring together city pop, jazz, indie pop and ambient sounds, drawing on both Tokyo’s underground music scene and French influences.

They also handle the entire recording process themselves, from writing and performing to mixing and mastering. Their music’s combination of grooves and spacious textures makes this a promising pick for listeners who enjoy the softer, dreamier corners of pop. Catch them on Friday evening and give yourself 45 minutes to settle into their world.

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by FORMULA 1 SINGAPORE GRAND PRIX (@f1nightrace)

Tickets can be purchased through the official Singapore Grand Prix website. Check that your ticket covers the day and access zone of your chosen performances. Plan accordingly and consult the official entertainment schedule before heading down.

Like what you read? Show our writer some love!

items.body: Helen Linda’s Head Ahoy! Liz Harris of Grouper draws up the anchor of her 2013 slowcore side project and sets sail once more with drummer Jed Bindeman on the high seas Linda's Head by Helen On 27th March 1980 Mt. St Helens erupted. Two months later, Liz Harris (AKA Grouper) was born. In 2013, she teamed up with drummer Jed Bindeman and Scott Simmon on bass, introducing the world to their shoegaze band Helen with the double A-side single ‘Felt This Way’ / ‘Dying All The Time’. Their dreamy debut The Original Faces followed two years after with the band subsequently laying dormant… until now. The reappearance of this Pacific Northwest slowcore trio a decade later is less an eruption, more a profusion. Or, better... The post Helen – Linda’s Head appeared first on The Quietus.

It's a strong + cohesive collection of stirrin' + bittersweet toons. My jam.The lyrics are relatable. The metaphors strong see Lake of MemoriesThe arrangements dynamic without too many surprises. The odd fluteor trumpet helps the diversity of soundsChris is still a nostalgic dude, seekin' consolation + inspirationNow. To put all this in context.I've been deep into Macca + Wings lately.Even the whimsical, twee stuff, Silly Love Songs, Waterfalls, With a Little LuckAll those cool sound effects Let 'Em In....The doorbell...the telephone broopsin Uncle Albert....but.....always deeply melodic, great bass lines...cool lyrics...Band on the Run.....no one comes close to Macca....by a long wayBut Chris comes closest. Inspired by Macca, Kate Bush. Squeeze, Tears for Fears,Prefab Sprout. Has he made A Deal with G-d (?) The band are tight, not too flashy, there are no Howes or Sherwoods or Schellens here,but Bainbridge always brings a yearnin' + keenin' quality to his Celtic tinged palette,there's some lovely fretless bass work...Geoff is there as the bedrock of the music.Electronic or orchestrated as the song calls for....This is a mature album in terms of themes.Sometimes self-helpy. Chris means well. Am sure he writes to reveal himself to his 2 boys.Most of the times it's that wry, hard-won bitter sweetness that I adore.Juliet is a real outlier....a personal narrative, Chris sings as if he is Anne Perry's brotheror cousin tryin' to understand why she dunnit...would this be a radio hit (?)"could you kill again?" "was it sin or was it bliss"...this dark horror theme, pertainin'to a woman is very Kate Bush-y......would love her to cover itThe singles are a rush. The ballads heart breakin'. Lake of Memories is magnificent.Someone has to play these LIVE...Almond is holdin' his 5 yearly Marc Bolan celebration.Be nice if they did Juliet at least.They have brought the drivin' grooverama + the creamy dreaminess !!! 💚....

items._cn_summary: 这是Geoffrey Downes与Chris Bainbridge合作的跨界前卫专辑，以成熟主题与苦涩的甜蜜感为核心。编曲动态而不张扬，辅以长笛和小号点缀丰富音色层次。Bainbridge的演唱带有凯尔特色彩与渴望感，贝斯线条流畅。歌词富有隐喻与叙事性，部分单曲节奏强劲，部分抒情曲令人心碎，尤其Lake of Memories被盛赞。整体制作精良，乐队配合紧密，但风格偏向主流旋律摇滚，缺乏实验性突破。

items.body: Review by Fercandio46 — There are times when reality is stranger than fiction, and the story behind the making of this album is another example of that. Philippe DeBarge was a young French heir to a pharmaceutical fortune and a huge fan of The Pretty Things. Guitarist Dick Taylor had become disillusioned by the lack of impact of S.F. Sorrow, leading Victor Unitt to join the band as his replacement; this was the first album he recorded with them. DeBarge contacted the musicians and invited them to his opulent ch�teau in Saint-Tropez to propose a deal: he would fund their stay and record an album with himself as the lead vocalist. There, at the Epi-Plage club and his own residence, a thoroughly bohemian gathering took place, reminiscent of a Fran�oise Sagan novel; French rock legend Johnny Hallyday and actress Brigitte Bardot mingled and played guitar amidst a black-and-white "Nouvelle Vague" atmosphere. The album was recorded in London at Nova Studios. Thanks to DeBarge's funding, The Pretty Things had access to high-quality equipment, including an 8-track tape recorder.After the recording sessions, DeBarge took the masters to France, and the material remained in storage, unreleased and forgotten, on acetate discs. The acetate has been bootlegged since then. In 2010, it was acquired by Mike Stax, owner of the 1960s music magazine Ugly Things. He unearthed one of the two acetates, had it mixed and mastered, and then, as a bonus track, It led the classic Pretty Things lineup, which Dick Taylor had just left at the time the tracks with DeBarge were recorded, to record a song titled "Monsieur Rock" (Philippe's Ballad) as a bonus track for this release on Ugly Things UTCD-2207.The songs "Alexander," "Eagle's Son," and "It'll Never Be Me" were already known, having been recorded in the late 1960s by "Electric Banana", the pseudonym under which The Pretty Things recorded soundtracks for De Wolfe Music. Notably, these three songs appear in Menahem Golan's film What's Good for the Goose (1969).The Philippe DeBarge album itself serves as a bridge between the group's major Works, S.F. Sorrow and Parachute, yet it stands on its own merits. Less dark than its predecessor, it is perhaps the final example of that fresh, unpredictable, exciting, and thrilling, yet fun, psychedelia. This is evident in the opening track, "Hello, How Do You Do," which echoes the trippier side of the Rolling Stones' Their Satanic Majesties era, while the restrained calm of "You Might Even Say" recalls the Kinks. The track "Alexandre" is vocally challenging, raw and pugnacious, reminiscent of the early Who, yet it takes flight thanks to the Pretty Things' backing vocals and Victor Unitt's diverse guitar solos; these solos explore various shades of psychedelia while occasionally channeling the wild spirit of his previous group, the Edgar Broughton Band.These tracks sit alongside others with a more pop-oriented sound, charming thanks to the use of the clavichord, as in "Send You With Loving," and a prominent bassline. The album's real strength lies in its garage-rock, almost proto-punk, tracks, which are packed with energy and vocal harmonies, blending acoustic Indian ethnic elements with rock 'n' roll piano, as heard in "You're Running You And Me." "Peace" possesses a unique poetry and beauty, and is linked to "Eagle's Son," carrying forward its infectious rhythm and energy. It features melodies full of personality, where the rock and pop of "Swinging London" float through, almost becoming anthems of the era.While the influence of the Beatles could be traced in FS Sorrow, here we find psychedelia driven by acoustic guitar and harpsichord, punctuated by bursts of distorted electric guitar in soundscapes closer to the Kinks. The work evokes an era when the past and the future did not clash, simply because they were distinct, as seen in "New Day." Wally Waller handles piano and organ duties on "It'll Never Be Me", a track that remains laid-back right up until Victor Unitt's screeching solo, while the bongo percussion adds a relaxing touch that contrasts with the album's more urgent moments."Monsieur Rock (Ballad Of Philippe)" sounds more modern yet fits the spirit perfectly; it is even moving, evoking an era where the backing vocals and guitar seem to pick up exactly where they left off. The sound is raw, defiant, and powerful, with an improvisational feel, making it a fitting tribute that brings a sense of currency and relevance to this long-awaited official release.Twink left in late 1969 to form Pink Fairies. Skip Alan returned on drums just in time for the band's return to Abbey Road to begin work on Parachute, which retained the psychedelic sound but incorporated increasingly progressive elements. And Philippe DeBarge shines like those teenage memories that, as time goes by, leave you wondering if they were real or imagined...distorted like that very psychedelia, a time capsule that endures like the eternally fair weather of the Saint-Tropez coast.
items._genre: psychedelic rock / proto-prog / garage rock
items._cn_summary: 这张专辑由法国富二代Philippe DeBarge资助，召集The Pretty Things在其圣特罗佩的庄园录制，最终由小型地下厂牌Ugly Things于2009年发行。制作背景颇具传奇色彩——录音借用了Nova Studios的高端8轨设备，部分曲目来自Electric Banana时期的影视配乐。音乐风格延续乐队S.F. Sorrow至Parachute之间的过渡阶段，保留了迷幻摇滚的实验余韵，吉他独奏在不同音色间游走，键盘与和声层次丰富。整体仍属英式迷幻摇滚的传统范畴，与用户关注的实验前卫、自由即兴、电子暗潮等方向存在较大距离。

items.body: Review by A Crimson Mellotron — Few late-80s metal albums are as influential as Savatage's fourth studio offering 'Hall of theMountain King', originally released by Atlantic. This is the first album by the American bandproduced by then-new producer Paul O'Neill, who had insisted on a more coherent musical direction,while also adding a bit of a conceptual edge to their recordings. At the same time, the band shows awillingness to experiment with more sophisticated arrangements and tighter compositions, as heardthroughout the album. The result is a darker, progressive-oriented record that sits at theintersection of melodic power metal and technical heavy metal, offering a triumphant and relentlesssound graced by fast-paced guitars and stunning vocal performances. As usual, fantastical elementsprevail on this Savatage album, bringing along an interesting aesthetic that sets the band apartfrom many of its contemporaries in the heavy metal scene. The lack of success of their previousalbums may have motivated Savatage to create a solid, kind of "bulletproof" collection of songs,that is what the record feels like.The straightforward songwriting, thunderous solos, and the overall dark atmosphere of 'Hall of theMountain King' render this album an appealing listen from start to finish. Its ten tracks areprimarily written by Jon and Criss Oliva, respectively lead singer and lead guitarist of the band,while a few songs also credit producer O'Neill as a co-writer. This record also has instrumentalarrangements of excerpts from 'In the Hall of the Mountain King' by Grieg and 'Mars, the Bringer ofWar' by Holst, which is further proof that Savatage were pursuing a sophistication of their soundwith this release. Opening side one is the song '24 Hrs. Ago'. Its sweeping, metallic riff providesa menacing and theatrical tone that is taken on by the following track 'Beyond the Doors of theDark', which is another really heavy and powerful composition. 'Legions' then explores a grooved uppower metal sound, while the melodic number 'Strange Wings' sees Savatage dialing back on the speedand aggression of the first three songs. Side two then follows up with the instrumental 'Prelude toMadness' and the iconic title track that needs no introduction. Of the four songs that follow andconclude the record, 'White Witch' and 'Devastation' impress as well-arranged ballsy metal pieces,while the instrumental interlude 'Last Dawn' is quite enjoyable. Of course, many of the progressiveelements are still underdeveloped on this release, while the instrumentals occasionally feel likestopgap entries in a sequence of songs mostly dedicated to powerful riffing and vocal bravado.Nevertheless, the vocals of Jon Oliva are fantastic all throughout 'Hall of the Mountain King',while the writing and the arrangements are really strong. The quality of the entire album isindicative of how Paul O'Neill understood what the band needed to become an 80s heavy metal majesty.And despite its minor imperfections, this 1987 record remains one of the most important entries inthe band's catalogue.
items._genre: progressive metal / power metal / heavy metal
items._cn_summary: Savatage 第四张录音室专辑由新制作人 Paul O'Neill 主导，乐队在旋律力量金属与技术重金属之间寻找更统一的表达方向。专辑整体氛围偏暗，前卫元素开始浮现，但评论明确指出这些前卫成分尚不成熟，器乐段落有时显得是衔接歌曲序列的填充。Jon Oliva 的人声表现强劲，吉他 riff 与独奏占据主导，曲目主要由 Oliva 兄弟创作，并融入格里格《山魔王》、霍尔斯特《火星》改编的器乐片段，体现对古典素材的引用企图。尽管专辑在八十年代金属乐坛具有影响力，并被视为乐队向后续更成熟前卫方向发展的起点，但其本质仍是结构清晰、以强劲 riff 与演唱为核心的金属作品，与实验、前卫爵士或电子音乐等领域的融合有限。

items.body: Independent Polish musician Sławek Stróżyk released the single “Tylko Ty” (“Only You”) on September 18, 2026, through distributor Crave Digital. The track places Polish-language male vocals in a synthwave/electro setting with a cyberpunk atmosphere, and explores closeness as a source of strength while the surrounding world changes. “Tylko Ty” runs 2 minutes and 47 seconds at 120 BPM. Stróżyk wrote the composition and lyrics, performed the track and handled its recording, production, mix and master himself in his home studio using Reaper. The original music and vocals involved no generative AI. “Tylko Ty” previously featured on the “Synthpop Symphony” podcast. The single is available to stream on Spotify, Apple Music and YouTube. About Sławek Stróżyk Sławek Stróżyk is an independent musician, composer, guitarist, vocalist and producer based in Poznań, Poland, with more than twenty years of experience spanning session performance, recording engineering and sound design. His solo work brings together synthwave and electronic production with a wider interest in pop, ballads and rock. Stróżyk records in his own home studio using Reaper, taking responsibility for the complete creative and technical process from composition through to the finished master. “Tylko Ty,” released September 18, 2026, is his latest single under that approach. Stróżyk is currently working on his debut solo album, with material spanning pop, ballads, rock and synthwave, continuing the independent, self-produced method behind “Tylko Ty.”
items._genre: synthwave / electro / synth-pop

items.body: Kontravoid has announced an extensive European run for November and December 2026, combining support dates with Boy Harsher and Choir Boy, a stop at Hellsinki Industrial Festival, a series of headline shows and a final stretch alongside Los Angeles EBM duo Spike Hellis. The tour also includes three Polish dates in Warsaw, Kraków and Poznań. The tour arrives just weeks after Kontravoid released the new ten-track album “Sound of the Void” on 2 October through Artoffact Records. The record follows 2024’s “Detachment” and includes tracks such as “Mortal”, “Chances”, “Returning” and the title track. Sound of the Void by Kontravoid The first part of the European run begins on 14 November at Le Transbordeur in Lyon, where Kontravoid joins Boy Harsher and Choir Boy. Dates follow in Paris, Strasbourg, Frankfurt, Lausanne, Munich and Vienna. Boy Harsher’s own schedule confirms Choir Boy across these European shows. Kontravoid then breaks away on 21 November for Hellsinki Industrial Festival, where the Saturday bill also includes Gothminister, Das Ich, Ambassador21 and others. After further headline dates through Greece, Italy and Switzerland, Kontravoid returns in December for another run, this time with Spike Hellis. That section reaches Hamburg, Copenhagen, Berlin and then Poland, with shows at Mechanik in Warsaw on 11 December, Gwarek in Kraków on 12 December and Pod Minogą in Poznań on 13 December. The Poznań date is already confirmed as a Kontravoid and Spike Hellis bill, while the Kraków show has also gone on sale as part of the Europe Fall 2026 tour. Tour dates for Kontravoid 14.11 – Lyon, FR – Le Transbordeur * 15.11 – Paris, FR – Bataclan * 16.11 – Strasbourg, FR – La Laiterie * 17.11 – Frankfurt, DE – Zoom * 18.11 – Lausanne, CH – Docks * 19.11 – Munich, DE – Kesselhaus * 20.11 – Vienna, AT – Ottakringer Brauerei * 21.11 – Helsinki, FI – Hellsinki Industrial Festival 23.11 – Thessaloniki, GR – The Host 24.11 – Athens, GR – Death Disco 26.11 – Pisa, IT – Caracol 27.11 – Bologna, IT – Freakout 28.11 – Messina, IT – Retronouveau 30.11 – Zurich, CH – Xtra-Musikcafé 05.12 – Rotterdam, NL – Baroeg ** 06.12 – Paris, FR – Le Chinois ** 08.12 – Hamburg, DE – MS Stubnitz ** 09.12 – Copenhagen, DK – BETA ** 10.12 – Berlin, DE – Cassiopeia ** 11.12 – Warsaw, PL – Mechanik ** 12.12 – Kraków, PL – Gwarek ** 13.12 – Poznań, PL – Pod Minogą ** * with Boy Harsher and Choir Boy ** with Spike Hellis About Kontravoid Kontravoid is the solo project of Cameron Findlay, mixing darkwave, EBM, industrial electronics and club music. Findlay’s masked live presence has become part of the project’s visual identity, but the music stays built for direct physical impact: rigid bass sequences, heavy electronic percussion and melodies that often cut through the harsher production with unusual clarity. “Sound of the Void” is Kontravoid’s second full-length for Artoffact Records and contains ten tracks. Kontravoid’s North American tour with Buzz Kull ran earlier in 2026, and Side-Line covered the new album’s announcement in September (Kontravoid announces new album ‘Sound Of The Void’, shares single ‘Without’) ahead of its 2 October release (Kontravoid releases new album ‘Sound Of The Void’). About Boy Harsher Boy Harsher, the duo of Jae Matthews and Augustus Muller, enter the European dates with a new album of their own. “GET MEAN” was released on 18 September 2026 and contains twelve tracks. The record deals directly with grief, heartbreak and survival. It keeps the duo’s characteristic combination of minimal electronics, coldwave and physically insistent club rhythms. Their European tour begins in Lyon on 14 November and continues through France, Germany, Switzerland, Austria, the Netherlands and the UK. About Choir Boy Choir Boy began as the project of vocalist and songwriter Adam Klopp, with the current line-up also including Chaz Costello, Jeff Kleinman and Michael Paulsen. The band’s sound sits on the softer edge of the tour’s spectrum, built from dream pop, new wave and romantic synth-pop. In April 2026 they released the single “I’ll Always Let You Down”, written by the full band with Jorge Elbrecht and described by Klopp as an “anti-love song”. About Spike Hellis Los Angeles duo Spike Hellis bring the December dates back toward harsher body music. Their second full-length, “Successor”, was released on 7 August 2026 and follows their 2022 self-titled debut. The ten-track record includes “By God”, “Your Successor”, “Unwound (Get Right)” and “Entirely Mine”. It keeps the duo’s stripped, physical combination of EBM, industrial electronics and minimal synth. The duo describe their sound as “body music to hijack the amygdala.”

items.body: 音楽家の三宅純がスコアを手がけた、映画『Oxygen Station（オキシジェン・ステーション）』のサウンドトラックがリリース決定。 映画『Oxygen Station』は、2023年に制作されたウクライナ、チェコ、スロバキア、スウェーデンの共同制作による伝記ドラマ映画で、クリミア・タタール民族指導者として知られるムスタファ・ジェミレフ（Mustafa Dzhemilev）の生涯が描かれている。 監督はウクライナのイヴァン・ティムチェンコ（Ivan Tymchenko）。本作でウクライナ最高峰の国家映画賞であるゴールド・ズィーガ賞や、 オデッサ国際映画祭などでも受賞を果たしている。   なお、2026年10月13日（火）には 晴れたら空に豆まいて（東京都渋谷区）にてトークイベント『三宅純の広告音楽 CM TRACKS vol.2』が開催される。同イベントは、三宅純がこれまでに手がけてきたCM音楽を「広告」というコンテクストから切り離し、純粋な音楽作品として掘り下げる企画で、三宅本人が楽曲を解説。『Oxygen Station』のサウンドトラックも試聴予定で、同作の音楽制作にまつわるエピソードも聞ける貴重な機会となる。 三宅純 / 『オキシジェン・ステーション』オリジナル・サウンドトラック 2026/10/09 発売 投稿 三宅純が手がけたウクライナ映画『Oxygen Station』オリジナル・サウンドトラックが配信リリース は ARBAN に最初に表示されました。

items._cn_summary: 本文为新闻稿性质的内容，介绍音乐家三宅纯为乌克兰传记电影《Oxygen Station》所创作的配乐原声带发布信息。该电影以克里米亚鞑靼民族主义者穆斯塔法·杰米列夫生平为题材，由多国联合制作并获得乌克兰国家电影金奖项。文章主体侧重于电影背景、导演信息及发行渠道，并附带三宅纯CM音乐赏析活动的预告。原文未涉及配乐的具体作曲技法、配器选择、声音设计或音乐风格的深入分析，作为乐评缺乏实质性的音乐评论内容。

items._cn_summary: 这是一档名为Race The Sky的广播节目，由Cliff Furnald主持，内容涉及来自欧洲、亚洲、北美与南美等地的跨地域音乐选播。节目以藻类为主题概念，强调无类型界限的选曲逻辑。从现有描述来看，这是一档汇集多地区、多风格的世界音乐拼盘式电台节目，并非聚焦于特定艺术家的专辑评论。由于缺乏对具体音乐技法、编曲细节或艺术意图的深入剖析，信息量极为有限。节目在世界音乐方向上有一定涉及，但整体更偏向广播节目导览而非真正意义上的专辑乐评，原创评论深度不足，无法为听众提供关于声音设计、演奏特征或创作背景的有效参考。
